#### [Chorus: Shared N-gram Embeddings with Layer-wise Adaptation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.23386>)

Chorus’s new experimental report tests sharing n-gram memory across a language model while letting each layer rescale and project the shared features for its current state. Matched small-model comparisons show lower validation loss and selective recall gains with smaller memory tables, offering a way to expand stored knowledge without duplicating a table at every read layer.

#### [Training agents for professional work when success is rare](<https://snorkel.ai/blog/gdpval-agents-rare-success/>)

Snorkel’s new professional-task study evaluates an existing binary-gated policy-gradient recipe that uses graded feedback only when every attempt in a rollout group fails. ### 2.7 Agent Harness &amp; Reliability

#### [SkillBridge: Cost-Aware Diagnosis and Repair of Cross-OS Compatibility Defects in Agent Skills](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26256>)

SkillBridge treats an agent skill’s guide, scripts, metadata and dependencies as one operating-system contract, using static evidence to prioritize runtime diagnosis and targeted repairs. A reviewed replay study and retrospective validation-budget analysis show how this evidence chain can improve target-system task completion while concentrating expensive checks on likely compatibility problems. The judgments come from agents, and the repairs were not consistently retested on other previously working systems, so the evidence supports scoped target-system improvements rather than general portability guarantees.

### 3.3 Inference Engines &amp; Serving

#### [Aggron: Aggressive Compression of Agentic KV Caches during Head-of-Line Stalls in the Request Queue](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.26435>)

Aggron compresses an agent’s prose tail while its request waits for KV-memory admission, retaining the latest protected tool-output prefix and using a separate summary queue plus a latency predictor to hide compaction behind existing stalls. In trace-driven Qwen3.6-35B-A3B simulations at high offered load, it improves throughput by 1.34–1.40× and reduces program p99 latency by 27–31% against Slipstream and APEC, suggesting a practical way to turn admission delays into memory savings. Those system gains are simulated rather than measured under concurrent live Aggron traffic; separate live compression-arm quality checks have wide noise bands and do not prove adaptive-controller quality equivalence, while low-memory-pressure configurations can regress.

### 3.4 Attention, KV Cache &amp; Memory Systems

#### [Twindex: Index Cache Offloading with Coarse-to-Fine Selection for Long-Context Sparse-Attention Serving](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.25078>)

Twindex keeps compressed sparse-attention indexes in GPU memory, fetches a larger candidate pool from host memory and rescores it in the model’s native precision, reducing the index bottleneck after main-KV offloading without retraining model weights. At 992K-token prompts, it raises peak steady-state decode throughput by 1.25–2.54× over an equivalently optimized HiSparse baseline across three models on anonymized 179-GiB GPUs with TP4 or TP8. These gains trade larger batches for longer decode steps and depend on memory and prefix-sharing policies; they are not an end-to-end latency or exact global-selection guarantee, and a batched shared-index alternative narrows one Qwen comparison to about 1.04×.

Offline model-specific calibration/development tuning and sufficient host bandwidth/capacity are required; model weights are not retrained. Native rescoring is conditional on shortlist coverage and remains approximate globally. Full-HBM throughput comparisons use different concurrency and longer steps; Qwen/GLM headline prompts share98% main-KV prefixes. Index-sharing/scoring policy materially reduces the gain. Native Qwen top-k has an overflow quirk, separately controlled. No SSD/remote-tier experiment, full fresh-traffic1532-request run, general serving-cost result or quality-equivalence proof;1.5–2M Qwen checks use YaRN beyond supported context.

### 3.5 Kernels, Compilers &amp; Runtimes

#### [Inkling 2 Mini on vLLM: Per-Pass Caches and Variable-Loop Execution](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-20-inkling2-mini>)

vLLM’s Inkling2 Mini integration represents repeated core-layer visits as separate cache layers and fuses cross-pass message reads and gated controllers, supporting shared weights without incorrectly sharing each pass’s KV and convolution state. For the separate variable-loop research checkpoint on one GB200 at TP1 and 4K context, reducing three passes to one lowers batch-one forward decode-step time from 3.85 ms to 1.51 ms and raises KV capacity from 175K to 352K tokens; sharing KV across three passes instead yields 194K tokens with similar step time. These controls make loop execution and its memory tradeoffs inspectable, but are rejected by fixed-loop Inkling2 Mini, do not establish a quality–speed frontier and measure forward passes rather than end-to-end serving.

**Published:** 2026-11-20 · **First seen:** 2026-11-21T16:37:08.523+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Looped Models, Execution Runtime, KV Cache, Operator Fusion

[Blog](<https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-11-20-inkling2-mini>) · [Code](<https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/69028>) · [Project](<https://huggingface.co/thinkingmachines/TML-d24-varloop-research>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. Read the complete primary technical article and its immutable initial Markdown at blog commit c29cac02828531bb410100ca4e4b92acd0006080 (Nov20 20:18:15Z), including all mechanisms, variable-loop table and accuracy disclosures. Also read the complete launch-time loop controller (16257bytes) and relevant config option/cache-visit/DSpark validation sections; both immutable first-PR loop/config files are byte-identical to current files.24 unique layers comprise prelude0–5/core6–17/coda18–23; three core passes give48 visits. Each later pass restarts from prelude state and reads gated messages from the previous pass’s two blocks. Controllers stack four message streams for batched GEMMs; merges are FP32 with preserved normalization and fused kernels extended from Inkling2 Small. Separate per-pass KV and conv states appear as ordinary cache layers. Only TML-d24-varloop-research permits pass-count and shared-KV overrides; sharing overwrites each token’s earlier-pass keys/values but retains per-pass convolution states, and DSpark requires the checkpoint’s default visit count. Original table on oneGB200,TP1,4K,forward-only gives batch1/batch32 step ms1pass1.51/3.81,2passes2.67/5.92,3passes3.85/8.11,3shared3.86/8.10; capacity352K/233K/175K/194K. These are configurations of the research checkpoint, not fixed Mini ablations against other models. Article lists end-to-end evaluation names but supplies no task scores, intervals or quality-versus-passes curve; its bitwise claim applies only to MoE outputs given identical inputs, not the full model. The Nov20 dated initial technical article is eligible conservatively in Nov21’s local03 window. Public PR69028 was created Nov20 20:21:10Z and first commit b3c0ff75424ea9393ce2dbfd2e912bb19f7323f0 is Nov20 20:17:02Z, but main merged only Nov21 16:19:34Z AFTER cutoff. Later mutable PR-body validation and post-cutoff main-merge performance are deliberately excluded. Current source is linked for review; initial immutable files verify the cutoff mechanism. HF repository creation dates Nov17/18 do not establish public availability of complete checkpoints; the dated release/blog and public PR are the evidence. This is a distinct execution integration/table, not a duplicate model-architecture evaluation entry or a new invention of prior Inkling2 Small kernels. First\_seen is actual successful Nov21 vLLM catalog completion16:37:08.523409Z; copied Nov20 index lacks Mini. No source code, container or model was executed.

**Limitations:** Single-node GB200 TP1 forward microbenchmarks at4K, with no run-count/variance or serving-throughput study in the frozen article. Variable-loop controls belong to a separate research checkpoint; fewer passes/shared KV alter computation and have no quantified quality comparison here. Conv state remains per pass and limits KV-sharing savings. Fixed Mini rejects these options, DSpark requires fixed default visits, and whole-model bitwise equivalence is not claimed. Existing Small kernels are reused. Current PR body/main branch include post-cutoff updates; only initial article/file mechanisms and table support this entry.
